Direction: #36 — the strongest available model as a third set of eyes. This increment
makes true: **the adjudicator's only input is derived from one source per
fact, names the model and effort the dispatch actually declared, and carries

Product Intent: After this increment, an adjudication record's artifact size, file set,
territory and patch agree by construction; the judge's model tracks the
strongest tier available to this account without a code change, its
reasoning effort is declared rather than inherited, and both are stamped on
every verdict receipt from a mechanically-derived source; and the record
carries the approved plan's oracle sections at their approved commit, the
tier's decline citation, and each finding's full reviewer-authored text,
under a stated input budget. No rubric, role, or dispatch point changes.

plan adds a channel by which the dispatching session's prose reaches it.

the self-serve leash and the David gate.
- The guard's hook path reads no configuration (threat-model rule 5).
- Existing committed receipts and records remain loadable: `loadLoop` on
every PR that has receipts today must still return a usable state.
- `.agents/machinery.json`'s required shape. This plan adds no key to it, so
every enrolled consumer's existing file stays valid unchanged.
- The record's refusal discipline: a fact it cannot establish is a stated
refusal or a stated `null` with a reason, never a zero.
Settled Decisions: 1. **Artifact facts come from git, over the same range as the patch, and
both endpoints are validated first.** `artifact.files/added/removed`, the
file set `territory` classifies against, and `artifact.patch` are all
derived from git over `base...head` (the snapshot's `pr.base.sha` and
`pr.head.sha`). **Correcting a round-1 claim:** those shas are *not*
already required — `assertAdjudicationSnapshot` validates the PR number,
repository and capture metadata but neither sha; `changesSince` validates
the head only, for its own separate range; and `artifactDiff` deliberately
returns an "unavailable" marker rather than failing when an endpoint is
missing. That tolerance was harmless while the file list came from the
snapshot; it is not harmless once the same range is authoritative for
size and territory. So both endpoints are explicitly validated as full,
resolvable commits before the shared list is derived, with a refusal
naming which one failed — never a silent empty list from an incidental
git failure. One function yields the
file list; the three consumers read it. Disagreement is then
unconstructible, not merely tested for.
2. **That file list is lossless, and its parsing rules are stated.**
(Round 1.) It is read with `--numstat -z --no-renames`: `-z` because a
path with a space, a quote or a non-ASCII byte is otherwise C-quoted and
silently mis-compared against a finding's path; `--no-renames` because
rename detection reports only a rename's destination, which the record's
existing discovery already disables for the same reason, so a rename
appears as its add and its delete and both paths are in the set. Binary
files report `-` for both counts: they carry `added: null, removed:
null`, are counted in `files`, and are surfaced as `binaryFiles: <n>`
beside the totals, so a non-zero artifact can never present as zero
lines without saying why. A count that is neither numeric nor `-` is a
refusal, not a coerced zero.

`base !== head` and the git-derived file set is empty, the generator
refuses and names the two shas. A PR under review with no diff is not a
state this machinery meets; the shape signals a wrong base or head.
4. **Size counts exclude the machinery's own record files; territory does
not.** `files/added/removed` describe the artifact under review, so they
apply the same exclusion the patch applies. A finding anchored on a
receipt or record file is nonetheless *inside this PR's diff*, so
`territory` classifies against the full changed set, including both
sides of a rename. The record's `territory.note` states this, and the
size fields state the exclusion, so a reader cannot mistake one for the
other.
5. **The judge's model is declared once, in its own definition's
frontmatter, as `best` — the alias that resolves to the strongest model
available to this account.** Verified against the Claude Code
documentation (see *External-claim verification*): `best` "uses the
latest Fable model where it's available to you, otherwise the same model
as `opus`", and subagent frontmatter accepts the same values as the
`--model` flag. This is what David asked for on 2026-09-06 — the
strongest model, tracked without a PR when that changes — and it is
strictly better than the alias-in-config design this plan carried at
round 1, because it needs no configuration key at all, tracks *across*
tiers rather than within one, and degrades to Opus rather than failing
if Fable is ever unavailable. Consequently **the dispatch passes no
per-invocation `model`**: this harness's Agent tool exposes `model` as a
four-alias enum that does not include `best`, so passing anything there
would override the frontmatter and pin the tier — the exact defect being
removed. The guard's refusal text and every routing instruction change
from naming a tier to naming the definition file.

first step is an empirical check that this harness accepts `best` in
subagent frontmatter. If it does not, the declared value is `fable`.
(Round 2.) Everything downstream is written against **the empirically
selected alias**, not against the literal `best`: the class-1 oracle
asserts exactly one declarative pin naming *that* alias, the runtime
fixture asserts `dispatch.model` equals *that* alias, and the Definition
of Done reads the same way — so the fallback cannot produce an
implementation that fails the plan's own acceptance checks. The fallback
path gets its own test: with `best` unavailable, a `fable` declaration
and its stamps are accepted. The mechanism under review is the
frontmatter being the single declaration, not the particular alias in
it.
6. **The judge's reasoning effort is declared in the same frontmatter, not
inherited.** `effort: xhigh`. Verified: subagent frontmatter accepts
`low | medium | high | xhigh | max`, overrides the session level,
inherits it when omitted, and has no per-invocation equivalent. Today
the adjudicator inherits, so its depth silently tracks the dispatching
session — an unpinned variable in a judge whose verdicts are audited.
`xhigh` rather than `max`: the judge's measured failure was applying a
rule to a situation nobody read, which is a depth failure, and a verdict
is ~0.1% of a loop's tokens; but `max` is documented as prone to
overthinking, and on a default-stop rubric overthinking reads as
manufactured reasons to continue.
7. **The record carries the dispatch declaration, read mechanically from
the definition file at the reviewed head, through a layout-aware
resolver.** (Round 1; the resolver added round 2.)
`dispatch: {model, effort, source, sha}` is parsed from the agent
definition's frontmatter at `snapshot.pr.head.sha` — never from the
working tree, never from anything the session types. The record is
generated before the dispatch and is the input the verdict cites, so this
is the same evidence chain every other record field uses.
**The resolver is not a bare `git show <head>:<consumer path>`**, because
the two layouts this machinery runs in disagree about where payload
lives: in the handbook, `.claude/agents/review-loop-adjudicator.md` is a
**symlink** (mode `120000`, whose blob is the target path text, not
frontmatter) and the tracked source is `core/.claude/agents/…`; in an
assembled consumer the same path is a regular file and no `core/` prefix
exists. So every head-pinned payload read goes through one resolver that
(a) reads the tree entry's **mode**, (b) follows a `120000` entry's
target relative to the link's directory, refusing a target that escapes
the repository or a chain deeper than one link, and (c) if the consumer
path is absent entirely, retries once under the `core/` prefix. A path
that resolves in neither layout is a refusal naming both attempts. This
applies equally to `declineCitation` (decision 11), whose consumer path

exist in the handbook at all — its tracked source is `core/.agents/…`.

compares them to the record — not to current configuration.** The
adjudication receipt carries `modelRequested` and `effortRequested`; the
validator resolves the `recordPath` the receipt already cites, reads
that record's `dispatch`, and refuses on any mismatch. A typed, stale or
invented value is therefore rejected without consulting anything mutable,
which was the round-1 defect: a non-empty-string check accepts fiction.
**Compatibility is decided by the cited record's schema, not by a date.**
(Round 2, replacing a cutoff constant.) A receipt must carry the stamps
**iff the record it cites carries `dispatch`**; a receipt citing a
pre-`dispatch` record is legacy and passes without them. A date cannot
work here: this plan-review PR never merges, so it has no merge date, and
the implementation PR cannot know its own merge date in advance — every
receipt written while that PR is itself under review would classify as
legacy, which is precisely the window the validator most needs to cover.
A date would also let a receipt with a copied-forward `decidedAt` bypass
the comparison, which is the operator mistake this validator exists to
catch. Keying on the record's schema is durable evidence and cannot be
backdated.

validators, with the merge gate performing the same record-derived check
against the committed record the receipt cites.
9. **What remains an assertion is named as one.** Nothing observable from
the harness proves the Agent tool actually served the declared model and
effort: the tool result carries no model id, and `get_session` describes
the main session, not a subagent. Decisions 5–8 establish *what the
dispatch declared*, verifiably and mechanically; they do not establish
*what ran*. The adjudicator's existing instruction to self-report a
mismatch stays as best-effort, and this residue is recorded as a known
gap rather than papered over.
10. **The record gains `planOracle`, sourced from the approved commit, and
absence is a refusal rather than a null.** (Refusal added round 1.) The
PR body's *Approved-plan source* line is parsed for a commit sha (the
single-PR form `final plan commit <sha>`, or the combined form
`combined plan commit <sha>`). The generator resolves **the plan file the cited
commit itself introduced or modified** — `git diff-tree` against that
commit's parent, restricted to `docs/plans/PLAN_*.md` — rather than
every plan file present at that commit, because a repository may
legitimately retain an older plan on `main` (the loop permits it when
David asks), which would make an "exactly one file present" rule refuse
every future plan. Zero or two *introduced* plan files is a refusal
naming the commit; a pointer carrying an explicit path uses it directly.
It then copies the *Direction*, *Product Intent*, *Must Not Change* and
*Settled Decisions* sections verbatim, with the sha. The
body supplies only the pointer; the text comes from the pinned commit,
which David's approval fixed and the builder cannot revise mid-loop.
`planOracle: null` is produced **only** when the body positively matches
one of the permitted no-plan forms — the bugfix tier oracle, the

with a line the parser cannot resolve, is a **refusal**: the contract
treats a missing approved-plan source as a finding in its own right, so
a record that silently proceeded without the oracle would hide exactly
the defect phase 1b exists to catch.
10a. **A `[PLAN REVIEW]` loop is its own positive form, and its oracle is
the plan file at the reviewed head.** (Round 2. Without this, decision

reviewing this plan — because a plan under review has no approved-plan
source by definition: it is not approved yet, and the loop's own
template has no such field.) The mode is detected from the PR body's

makes mandatory. In that mode `planOracle` carries

11. **The record gains `declineCitation`, tier-selected and read at the

# The machinery's threat model is my own mistakes, not an adversary — a local script is not a security boundary
## What happened
Making the review-budget guard and the readiness gate portable meant
replacing two hardcoded literals — the repository's `owner/name` and the
list of required CI jobs — with configuration. That is a configuration
problem. It was treated as a security problem, and it grew into one.
Each round of review asked "what if the working tree is edited before this
read?", "what if a same-numbered PR from another repository supplies its
snapshot?", "what if the branch commits a weaker policy than `main`?" — and
each answer moved the read somewhere harder to reach: from the working tree
to the durable ref, from the durable ref to the base commit, from a config
value to the budget receipt beside it. By round ten there were three
different trust anchors for one identity, a classification file ranking
their trustworthiness, and Codex was correctly finding the gaps *between*
the anchors, which is a combinatorial space. Every finding was real under
its own premise. The premise was wrong.
The premise was that the scripts must resist the person running them. In
this environment there is exactly one actor: the agent that edits the
working tree, commits to the branch, captures the snapshot, runs the gate
and posts the review request. Whatever it can "attack" it can also simply
not run. The controls that exist against deliberate action are outside the
scripts entirely — a human's merge click, and the server-side ruleset on
`main` — and no local hook can add to them, because the hook's operator is
the party being controlled.
## What worked instead
State the job plainly and design for it: **the identity checks catch
mistakes.** Declaring a budget in the wrong checkout. Capturing the wrong
PR's snapshot because every repository has a #7. Running a gate in a
consumer that still carries the seed placeholder. Those are the failures
that actually happen, and every one is caught by the same simple shape:
1. **One reader.** `.agents/machinery.json` is read from the working tree,
because it is configuration and that is where configuration lives. One
function reads it; it fails closed on absent, malformed, or placeholder.
2. **Stamp on mint, compare on consume.** Every artifact the machinery
writes carries `repo` from that config. Every artifact it reads is
compared to it. A mismatch refuses with "minted for X, you are in Y."
3. **GitHub's word is compared to config too.** A snapshot naming another
repository is refused: you captured the wrong PR.
4. **No trust hierarchy.** Not "base commit beats durable ref beats working
tree." One source, compared everywhere. (Receipts are still read from
the durable ref — for *durability*, so a decision survives the container,
which is a different concern that predates this one.)
5. **The guard path reads no config**, for an operational reason, not a
trust one: an exception escaping the hook exits 1 and the tool call
proceeds. There, the budget receipt is the anchor.
A finding of the shape "an edit to the working tree could…" is declined by
pointing here. It is not a defect in a mistake-catcher that its operator can
disable it.
## Takeaway
Before hardening a check, name the actor it is hardening against. If the
answer is "the person who runs it," stop: you are designing a lock whose key
is on the same ring, and every layer you add is a place for two copies of
the same value to disagree. Ask instead what mistake the check catches, make
it catch that mistake in one obvious way, and put the real control — a
human's approval, a server-side rule — where a local script cannot reach it.

body: **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep nested headings inside oracle sections**

When an approved oracle section contains a nested heading (for example, `## Must Not Change` followed by `### Security`), this condition stops at that nested heading and silently omits the heading and every constraint beneath it. Markdown sections end at a heading of the same or higher level, so the resulting record can hide load-bearing, human-approved invariants from the adjudicator and produce a verdict against an incomplete source of truth. When a PR body merely contains text such as `final plan commit abc1234`, this regex accepts it even without an `Approved-plan source` field, plan-review PR number, or David approval date; the phrase can also occur anywhere else in the body. `planOracleFor` then labels the commit's plan as approved instead of refusing malformed provenance, allowing the sole adjudicator input to present an unapproved or ambiguously sourced plan as authoritative. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guarantee progress while enforcing the record cap**

When a serialized record remains over 600,000 characters after the first total-cap truncation, the selected body's replacement is itself a non-empty truncation marker, so the next iteration selects the same item again and can loop forever. If oversized metadata leaves no non-empty body, the adjacent `break` instead returns a record above the advertised cap; thus sufficiently large review histories can hang record generation or overflow the adjudicator's input budget in every synced consumer.

When the new generator reads an older reviewed head whose adjudicator definition has no `effort` field, it emits a modern `dispatch` block with `effort: null`. This branch skips the comparison entirely, so an omitted or invented `effortRequested` value passes both the review-budget guard and merge gate even though the receipt documentation requires every modern stamp to equal the cited record; only records with no `dispatch` block should receive legacy treatment.
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove stale Fable claims from live tripwire guidance**

After this rewritten step delegates model selection to the definition's `best` alias, the immediately following operator instruction still calls the verdict “Fable's recommendation” (`core/scripts/review-budget.mjs:1662`), and the same obsolete fixed-tier claim remains in `core/.claude/skills/pr-watch/SKILL.md:72` and `core/.agents/receipts/README.md:161`. When `best` falls back to Opus, these live instructions report the wrong judge to both the agent and David, contradicting the receipt's new declaration-based audit trail; update the remaining operational descriptions along with the routing change.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept the documented bugfix oracle shape**

When a bugfix reaches the mandatory round-3 adjudication, its documented PR body contains `Fix tier`, `Reported symptom`, `Intended correct behavior`, `Must not change`, `Root cause`, and `Blast radius` (`core/.claude/skills/bugfix/SKILL.md:244-259`), not an inline `Approved-plan source: n/a — bugfix` line. This matcher therefore misses a correctly formed bugfix PR, and `planOracleFor` throws before the required adjudicator can run, leaving the review loop unable either to write the next fix or close on a verdict.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the plan path to its provenance line**

When the PR body mentions any `docs/plans/PLAN_*.md` outside the `Approved-plan source` field—for example, in copied Product Intent or a follow-up-plan reference—this body-wide match selects the first such path and bypasses `planFilesIntroducedBy`. If that file exists at the cited commit, the record silently presents the wrong plan sections as the approved oracle; if it does not, mandatory adjudication fails during `git show`. Extract the path only from the provenance line and verify it against the cited commit's plan candidates.
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the remaining live Fable routing claim**

Fresh evidence after the prior stale-copy fix remains at `core/.claude/skills/model-routing/SKILL.md:110-112`: the live “Routing work down” section still says the per-round adjudicator runs on Fable. That contradicts this new `best` rule whenever Fable is unavailable and the alias resolves to Opus, leaving agents and David with conflicting model and cost guidance; update that remaining claim to strongest-available routing.
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute the size after adding truncation metadata**

Fresh evidence after the prior cap-loop fix is that `serializedChars` is captured before `truncation.note` and the final size field are added, and the record is never serialized again. A record near the boundary can therefore exceed the declared total without `overCap` being set—for example, a 599,575-character metadata field records 599,726 characters while the returned pretty-printed JSON is 600,011—so the judge can still receive an silently oversized input and the audit field reports the wrong size. Add all metadata before the final cap check and measure the exact emitted serialization.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the plan-review oracle from the PR body**

On a `[PLAN REVIEW]` round, this extracts the oracle sections from the plan file itself rather than from the PR body's separate stated intent. If a revision drops or changes a Product Intent, Must Not Change, or Settled Decision, the adjudicator consequently receives the revised plan as both artifact and oracle and cannot detect the mismatch, even though plan reviews must check the specification against the PR-body intent. Preserve the head plan as the artifact, but populate the oracle from `pr.body`. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL130-L134](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/4bc165b1305c6333d79491d47a63dc6aa85c17f8/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#LL130-L134)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove the remaining Fable gate instruction**

Fresh evidence after the prior stale-copy fix remains in the checked merge fallback: `core/scripts/pr-ready.mjs:1810` still tells operators that a spent David grant requires a “fresh Fable recommendation,” while this declaration now routes the judge through `best` and may resolve to Opus. Following that live refusal can therefore pin the wrong judge while the receipt still claims the record's `best` declaration; `core/scripts/check-contract-consistency.mjs:103,120-121` also recommends the retired Fable-specific wording. Update these remaining operational messages to require the adjudicator declared by its definition.

When a valid snapshot identifies comments through a stable `PRRT_…` thread ID but its `html_url` lacks a `#discussion_r…` suffix, this new check rejects record generation before `fromMcp` runs. That is an explicitly supported snapshot shape in `core/scripts/__tests__/review-counting.test.mjs:404-416`, and `assertMcpSnapshotShape` deliberately falls back to the stable thread ID; rejecting it only in the adjudication generator can deadlock a mandatory round because the loop can neither obtain a continue verdict nor close on a stop. Accept the existing stable-thread-ID fallback here as well, or change the shared snapshot contract consistently.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep capped record fields readable by the adjudicator**

When one finding, plan section, or decline citation approaches these caps, `JSON.stringify` escapes its embedded newlines and emits the entire value as one JSON line. The adjudicator has only the `Read` tool, whose per-line limit cannot recover the remainder; the committed `.agents/receipts/loop-extension-38-1.json` already records this exact failure for the similarly serialized `artifact.patch`. Consequently, a value can remain below every declared cap, leave `truncation.fields` empty, and still be unavailable to the sole decision-maker, potentially hiding the critical finding or invariant that should cause `continue`; chunk these values into independently readable lines or cap each serialized line to the transport limit.

For a private/manual implementation PR, this accepts any `Approved-plan source` line containing the word `shasum`—even `Approved-plan source: shasum` with no filename, digest, or David approval date—and `planOracleFor` then returns a permitted null instead of its missing-source refusal. Those fields are the only independently inspectable provenance on the private path, so an incomplete or placeholder source is silently treated as evidence of an approved plan; require the documented filename, concrete hash, and approval date before selecting this form. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL39-L41](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/a6c0cc7d045fec053639a6c69885d945f8debd2b/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#LL39-L41)
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require immutable full SHAs for artifact endpoints**

When the manually assembled snapshot contains an abbreviated SHA or symbolic ref such as `HEAD` or `main`, this validation accepts it because `git cat-file` resolves any commit-ish; I confirmed both symbolic forms pass here. The subsequent artifact range and `dispatchDeclaration(head)` can therefore read the checkout's current branch rather than the PR commits captured from GitHub, while the record stores the mutable spelling as if it were pinned, allowing the sole adjudicator input to describe unrelated code. Require both endpoints to be full 40-character object IDs before resolving them.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve plan files when the reviewed head is a merge**

When an already-pushed plan-review branch merges newly landed `main`—the repository's required alternative to rebasing—the reviewed head is a merge commit, and this command returns no changed paths because it omits merge traversal. `git diff-tree -h` documents `-m` as “show diffs for merge commits”; without it, `planOracleFor` sees zero introduced plans and refuses the mandatory adjudication even though the PR still contains exactly one plan, leaving the loop unable to obtain either a continue or stop verdict. Derive the plan from the PR range or inspect and deduplicate the merge parents.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require complete approval provenance before trusting a plan**

When an implementation PR contains only `Approved-plan source: final plan commit abc1234`, this regex accepts it without the required plan-review PR number or David approval date, so any resolvable plan commit is presented to the adjudicator as approved. Fresh evidence after the claimed anchor fix is the regression fixture at `core/scripts/__tests__/review-loop-record.test.mjs:859`, which explicitly accepts this incomplete form; validate the full public provenance shape before selecting the commit. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL39-L41](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/ce77f336992c94b7ff80e6ce65916cb156fd0e64/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#LL39-L41)
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Select the plan from the plan-review side of a merge**

When a plan-review branch introducing `PLAN_A.md` merges a newer `main` that independently introduced `PLAN_B.md`, `diff-tree -m` emits `PLAN_B.md` against the branch parent and `PLAN_A.md` against the main parent, so deduplication still leaves two candidates and mandatory adjudication refuses. Fresh evidence beyond the prior merge fix is this two-parent topology—the added test only models the same plan repeated against both parents; derive candidates from the PR side/range or otherwise distinguish which parent supplied the reviewed plan.
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable rename detection for the artifact patch too**

When the PR renames a file, this numstat source deliberately reports the source and destination as separate delete/add entries, but `cappedDiff` generates `artifact.patch` without `--no-renames`; Git's help defines that flag as “disable rename detection,” and an identical rename is therefore emitted as one zero-line rename by the patch while `artifact` reports two files and all lines added/removed. Because the adjudicator weighs both size and patch, apply the same rename setting to the raw patch command so the newly unified artifact facts actually agree.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate dispatch stamps throughout the receipt chain**

When a valid terminal ship receipt follows an earlier adjudication receipt whose `modelRequested` or `effortRequested` disagrees with its cited record, this call validates only the terminal candidate; the subsequent `preceding` loop merely parses older receipts and checks terminal-verdict ordering. `loadLoop` rejects the earlier malformed receipt and therefore the entire loop, but `checkAdjudicatedCodex` can still return readiness from the terminal receipt, so run the record-derived stamp check for every preceding adjudication receipt as well.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the complete bugfix oracle block**

When a bugfix body contains only `**Fix tier:** C`, or a Tier A/B line followed by just `Reported symptom` or `Root cause`, these expressions accept it as a permitted no-plan form; they even accept an arbitrary tier such as `Z` in the A/B branch. The documented schemas at `core/.claude/skills/bugfix/SKILL.md:249-272` require all six Tier A/B fields or all five Tier C fields, and no other validator checks them, so the mandatory adjudicator receives `planOracle.sections: null` for a malformed or placeholder oracle instead of record generation refusing it. Validate the complete tier-specific block before selecting the no-plan path.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prefer an explicit approved-plan source over incidental no-plan text**

When a feature PR has a valid `Approved-plan source` but also quotes or demonstrates a bugfix/trivial form elsewhere in its body—for example, a process change containing `**Fix tier:** C`—this body-wide search runs first and returns `planOracle: null` without ever parsing the approved-plan commit. The sole adjudicator input then silently loses the human-approved oracle even though its provenance is present. Bind no-plan forms to the actual oracle block, or resolve a valid approved-plan source before considering them.
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record artifact patch truncation in the truncation summary**

When `artifact.patch` exceeds `PATCH_CAP_CHARS`, `cappedDiff` has already cut it before `applyCaps` runs, but this function never adds `artifact.patch` to `truncation.fields`. The resulting record can therefore have an empty `fields` array while this note explicitly says that means nothing was withheld, even though the patch was truncated at 60,000 characters. Preserve the patch's truncation state in the summary or stop making the empty-array assurance.
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject dispatch blocks that omit their required model**

When a modern cited record is malformed as `dispatch: { effort: "xhigh" }`, the missing `dispatch.model` is converted to a null expectation and a receipt with no `modelRequested` passes; both the review-budget guard and merge gate rely on this helper. `dispatchDeclaration` itself refuses to generate a dispatch without a model, so this shape is corruption rather than a legitimate declaration and should fail closed instead of silently disabling the new model-stamp check.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Store a scalar capture time in round-check receipts**

When the newly supported per-collection `capturedAt` object is used, this validation succeeds, but `check()` stores the raw object as `receipt.capturedAt`; `validateCheckReceipt()` later calls `Date.parse(receipt.capturedAt)`, gets `NaN`, and refuses the next review request as stale. Thus the documented shared-snapshot workflow can generate a receipt that the guard can never consume; write `capturedAtRaw` (or teach every receipt consumer the object shape) instead.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require timestamps for every counted collection**

When object-form capture metadata omits a collection or gives it an invalid timestamp, this silently discards that entry and accepts the oldest remaining valid value. For example, a snapshot containing stale `reviews` plus `capturedAt: { issueComments: <now> }` passes `assertCountingSnapshot`, so the round check can mint a fresh receipt from undated, potentially stale review evidence and undercount spent rounds. Require valid timestamps for every collection consumed by the check before selecting the oldest.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip fenced code while scanning oracle headings**

When a plan or PR body contains a fenced Markdown example with an oracle-shaped heading before the real section, this scanner treats the example as a heading even though Markdown does not. Fresh evidence beyond the nested-heading fix is the fenced-code topology: a preceding fenced ```markdown block containing `## Must Not Change` makes `sectionOf` return the example and omit the later real invariants, so the adjudicator again receives the wrong approved oracle. Track fenced-code state while locating headings.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept the documented split-loop provenance form**

When an implementation cites a split plan using the documented plural form—for example, `Plan-review PRs #701 and #702, combined plan commit abcdef1 on plan-review/foo-combined, approved by David on 2026-09-01`—the `\bPR\s*#` prefix cannot match `PRs #`, so `planOracleFor()` reports that no approved-plan source exists and mandatory adjudication cannot run. The split-loop contract explicitly requires naming every subsystem PR plus the combined commit (`core/.agents/core/claude-core.md:453-457`), so parse that form separately rather than treating `final` and `combined` as interchangeable suffixes of the single-PR regex.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind captured URLs to the target pull request**

When an operator accidentally combines `reviews` or `issueComments` captured from another PR with this snapshot's target metadata, each foreign entry still passes because this check verifies only that its numeric ID agrees with its own URL fragment. The URL path itself identifies the foreign repository and pull number, but that evidence is ignored, so `fromMcp()` can count foreign passes and triggers into the adjudicator's `rounds` and `trend` while the record is labelled as the target PR. Parse each URL's repository and `/pull/<n>` path and require both to match `snapshot.repo` and `snapshot.pr.number`.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject null dispatch blocks instead of treating them as legacy**

When a cited record contains `"dispatch": null` (or `false`), this truthiness check classifies it as a legacy record and skips both stamp comparisons. Only records where the property is absent predate this schema; a modern record accidentally edited to null can therefore let unstamped or invented model/effort values pass both the review-budget guard and merge gate, despite the following code correctly rejecting other malformed dispatch blocks.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require capture times for every adjudication collection**

When an object-form `capturedAt` contains only a parseable `issueComments` timestamp, this check accepts the snapshot even though `reviews` and `reviewThreads` may be stale or undated. Those collections determine the record's round trend and finding text, so a fresh issue-comment timestamp can make an incomplete historical view look current to the sole adjudicator; validate the full set with `capturedAtDetail` and apply an age bound rather than checking only one collection.
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore fenced examples when detecting plan-review mode**

When an ordinary PR body quotes `## Review mode` followed by `plan review only` inside a fenced Markdown example, this regex sets the body signal while the non-prefixed title leaves the title signal false, so record generation refuses the PR as half-declared. Process/documentation PRs can legitimately show this template, and if their review reaches mandatory adjudication the loop cannot obtain either a continue or stop verdict; apply the same fence-aware heading scan used by `sectionOf`. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL130-L134](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/434298e628dcc8066941d4432ba4dcc9ef72da7c/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#LL130-L134)
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the documented private approval and SHA-256 digest**

When a private-plan source says only `PLAN_X.md shasum 0123456789abcdef 2026-09-06`, this pattern accepts it without `shasum -a 256`, a 64-character SHA-256 digest, or any statement that David approved it. That is weaker than the private provenance form specified at `core/.agents/core/claude-core.md:453-457`, so a placeholder or unrelated date can be treated as authoritative approval and cause the adjudicator to accept a null plan oracle. [core/.agents/core/agents-core.mdL111-L114](https://github.com/TheAnswerManIsHere/AI-Handbook/blob/434298e628dcc8066941d4432ba4dcc9ef72da7c/core/.agents/core/agents-core.md#LL111-L114)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require every subsystem PR in split-plan provenance**

When a split source contains `Plan-review PRs #701, combined plan commit ...`, this expression accepts it because `PRs?` is followed by only one required number. The split contract requires naming every subsystem PR, and the code's own example uses `#701 and #702`; accepting the singular/incomplete form discards the independently inspectable provenance for the omitted subsystem before treating the combined plan as approved.
